title: Design: Cost move window names the moved part and its vendor bill
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin (a user with every setting, See Financial Data included).
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide at 100% zoom.
  • Have Internal Work Orders turned on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Use a location that is connected to QuickBooks Online, with every ShopView Accounts row mapped.
  • Have a customer flagged as Internal customer, with one asset, and its default internal category left at General Internal.
  • Have a new internal work order for that customer with every line Complete and one special-order part (for example Caliper) whose vendor bill (for example VB-2041) was posted to Cost of Parts while the work order was billable, made for this test.
  • Open the attached picture iwo-flow1-20-7e-close-vendor-bill-cost-moves-v13.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open the internal work order.
  2. Click Close Work Order.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The work order opens.

Step 2:

  • A window "Close work order [number]?" opens over the Finance tab.
  • Above the "Moved from" row the window reads "A vendor bill on this work order was posted to another account. Closing moves that cost."
  • The item line names this work order's special-order part and its vendor bill: "[part name] (special order), vendor bill [bill number]" (for example "Caliper (special order), vendor bill VB-2041").

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-R2: “Two cases open a dialog before closing, each only when its case applies: (1) a no-charge work order whose category requires the original work order and has none: "Close work order [number]?" with the selects "Original work order *" and "Original line" of S2-R2, the warning "[Category] requires the original work order. Pick the earlier work order this job comes from, or Not in ShopView.", and the buttons Cancel and "Close Work Order", disabled until one is picked; Goodwill never shows this; (2) a vendor bill whose cost moves to another account at Close (S7-R4), at a location with an accounting integration: "Close work order [number]?" with one "Moved from [account] to [account] $[amount]" row per pair of accounts, the amounts added up, and the buttons Cancel and "Close Work Order", the same dialog Create invoice shows for a move (S7-R8).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Internal Work Orders · All flows v6" (https://claude.ai/artifact/5jHR3nLeDinzks1viREFuo), version 1794561577-f903 (its boards byte-identical to version 1794510020-d4ec, which redrew 15 boards for PRD v1.2/v1.3, read and rendered 12 Nov 2026; the other 152 unchanged since version 1794484794-2031; checked 13 Nov 2026): page "Flow 1 · Create and close", board "7e Close · vendor bill cost moves" (Flow 1 · Create and close).

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • iwo-flow1-20-7e-close-vendor-bill-cost-moves-v13.png

The design's own words:

  • “A vendor bill on this work order was posted to another account. Closing moves that cost.”
  • “Caliper (special order), vendor bill VB-2041”

Difference: register IWO-D57, closed by check (c): the design is the source where the PRD is silent. The lead sentence and the item line add to the window of S3-R2; nothing contradicts it.

In the item line, "Caliper" and "VB-2041" are the design's example data; the window names the work order's own part and vendor bill.
